data.gender_notes: Mukunda is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Lord of wealth and giver of boons
data.long_meaning: Mukunda is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Mukta’ which means ‘to be free’. The name is associated with Lord Vishnu and is believed to bestow wealth and blessings upon the bearer. It is also considered a name of Lord Krishna, who is known as the ‘giver of boons’. The name Mukunda carries the meaning “Lord of wealth and giver of boons” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mukunda usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wealth and giver of boons and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the attainment of liberation and inner peace.
data.etymology: Mukunda belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of wealth and giver of boons.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mukunda total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Mukunda lies in its association with Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna, two major deities in Hinduism. These deities are believed to have the power to grant liberation from the cycle of birth and death and bestow boons upon their devotees. Therefore, the name Mukunda is believed to bring spiritual strength and the promise of liberation to those who carry it. Additionally, the name represents the desirable qualities of the divine, such as love, wisdom, and compassion, which inspires spiritual growth and devotion.

historical_references.reference: Mukunda, also known as Vishnu Avatar Matsya, is one of the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu. He is believed to have appeared during the Satya Yuga, the first of the four stages of human civilization, to save the Earth from being flooded. The story begins when the king Manu, the progenitor of mankind, performs a great yajna (rite) to save the Earth from being destroyed by the demon Hiraanyaksha. During this yajna, the god Vishnu in the form of Matsya, the fish, appears to Manu and promises to save the Earth.

Another significant reference to Mukunda is in the Bhagavad Gita, where Lord Krishna is addressed as ‘Mukunda’ by Arjuna. Arjuna, disciple of Lord Krishna, is filled with grief over the impending war and the loss of his kinsmen. Lord Krishna reassures Arjuna and explains that those who take refuge in Him, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, attain liberation and attain the ultimate goal of life. Arjuna, consoled by Krishna’s words, addresses Him as Mukunda, meaning ‘the giver of salvation or liberation.’
